reviews.title: I wish I had read the reviews before subscribing.
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with my experience. My subscription automatically renewed for an entire year, and I contacted support as soon as I noticed the charge. I explained that I did not intend to renew and that I had not used the subscription after the renewal, but I was still unable to get a refund.

I even asked for a reasonable alternative: instead of refunding the entire amount, I asked if they could change my annual subscription to a monthly plan and refund the difference. Unfortunately, I was not given that option either.

I understand that companies have refund policies, but I expected more flexibility and better customer support, especially since I reached out immediately.

If you decide to use this app, please be very careful with the automatic renewal and cancellation date. Based on my experience, once the annual charge goes through, getting a refund or even changing to a different plan can be very difficult.

I hope the company improves how situations like this are handled.

reviews.title: Do Not Download - EVER
reviews.text:
I downloaded this app while attempting to set up a small camera my children received as a gift. Unfortunately, this was not the correct app for the product, and I did not realize I was authorizing a $79.99 annual subscription.

I never created an account, never meaningfully used the service, and contacted the developer immediately after discovering the charge. I was told that only Apple could issue a refund. After multiple discussions with Apple, I was informed that Apple had contacted the developer regarding the refund request and that the developer declined to approve a refund.

As a result, I was charged $79.99 for a service I never used and never intended to purchase. While I understand subscription policies exist, this outcome feels unfair given the mistaken download, lack of account registration, lack of usage, and immediate effort to resolve the issue.

As a California consumer, this experience raises concerns about transparency and customer expectations surrounding subscription purchases and refunds. 

I hope the developer reconsiders its position and provides a refund. Until then, I would encourage potential users to carefully review any subscription terms before downloading.

Apple used to be customer first - they are now revenue first. The Google Pixel is looking more appealing. 

I will be filing complaints as my children are shocked how unfair. If you’ve had a similar experience see below.  

California Department of Consumer Affairs

California’s primary consume

reviews.title: At least reach out to me
reviews.text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but I feel completely let down by this app and its developer support.

I originally purchased a yearly subscription on January 9th for around $80. While dealing with issues inside the app, I accidentally purchased a second yearly subscription on January 12th. Instead of extending my account to two years, both subscriptions expire at the exact same time next January. That means I essentially paid $160 for one year of service.

I contacted support requesting a refund for the duplicate purchase, which I believe is completely reasonable, but I’ve received little to no helpful response. What makes this even more frustrating is that the developer seems very interested in using my account data to study how the app is used, yet when it comes to helping an actual paying customer, I feel ignored.

To make matters worse, I am now locked out of the app entirely. It keeps asking me to verify my account, and even after verifying, it still won’t let me back in.

The app itself is actually very cool and has a lot of potential, but no app is worth this level of frustration — especially not after paying twice for the same subscription and being unable to access it at all.

Because of the poor customer support, lack of communication, and unresolved billing issues, I have to give this app 1 star.
